label: D1 after the previous trial reached S2 and went unrewarded, or reached S2 rarely after a1
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), and only when the previous trial ended in S2: after S2 went unrewarded (common or rare), or after a1 led rarely to S2 (rewarded or not). It never fires at D1 after reaching S1 (prev_state==1 with no reward gives 0 activations). It also does not fire after a2 led commonly to S2 and was rewarded. Magnitude is largest after a1 -> S2 rare and unrewarded (precision 0.93, 58% of activation mass on 36% of active steps). It is much weaker after a2 -> S2 common and unrewarded (12% of mass on 34% of active steps), and in between after a1 -> S2 rare and rewarded. Most missed activations are the window-first D1 (rel -3), where the previous trial is outside the window; adding prev_state == -1 raises dev mass recall to 0.98 but lowers precision. The predicate uses only observed history (previous state, choice and reward).

issues: Every factual claim checks out on dev. Zero activations at GO and D2. Zero activations at D1 when prev_state == 1, rewarded or not. After a2 led commonly to S2 and was rewarded, precision is 0.02 and mass recall 0.008. The a1-rare-S2-unrewarded case has precision 0.926 and mass recall 0.577 on 36% of active steps. The a2-common-S2-unrewarded case has precision 0.73 and mass recall 0.12 on 34% of active steps. The a1-rare-S2-rewarded case falls in between (precision 0.70, mass recall 0.13).
Test F1 is 0.795, below the 0.8 bar. Recording 'explained' anyway overrides the threshold. Test precision is 0.778, so about 22% of predicted steps never fire.

Systematic false-positive class: the feature depends on reward two trials back, not only on the previous trial. Restricting the predicate to D1 with tv('reward',-2) == 0 gives these precisions: a2-common-S2-unrewarded 0.52 (vs 0.90 when tv('reward',-2) == 1), a1-rare-S2-rewarded 0.285 (vs 0.935), a1-rare-S2-unrewarded 0.745 (vs 0.996). Together these account for about 8k of the 14k dev false positives. The label and explanation do not mention this dependence on reward two trials back.

Systematic misses: nearly all are the window-first D1 (rel -3), where prev_state is not available. Outside rel -3, steps where the predicate is false hold only 2.5% of active steps and 0.8% of mass, so the rule is close to complete there. Adding only (prev_state == -1) & (prev_reward == 0) gives test F1 0.801 and mass recall 0.975. That is better than the agent's choice of all prev_state == -1 (F1 0.62), which the agent rejected.
Tightening the predicate with the reward two trials back raises precision (0.88-0.91) but lowers recall, so test F1 does not improve (0.75-0.78). The modulation is graded, not a clean rule.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after the previous trial reached S2 and went unrewarded, or reached S2 rarely after a1. Strongest after a1-rare-S2-unrewarded, and stronger when the trial before that was rewarded.
